items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: early on were Bill Holman, I loved that linear writing that he did

ctx.x: I forgot.. I made a pun and I didn’t know it. MR. Well, Don, I think that there’s probably a significant number of saxophone players in this country who have a kind of a love-hate relationship with you.

It’s cool. As long as they — it doesn’t matter. You know the saxophone parts, it’s nothing, everything that I’ve written I’ve played. It’s all based on my small group concept, all my big band charts. Everything. It’s a mood that I’ve experienced on the bandstand and I’ve translated it to the big band, you know, to be able to organize it in that sense. I started writing in Buffalo a long time ago. I was always very inquisitive. I wanted to know how does he get that sound, how does he make that, how does he do…
He’s a workaholic is what he is.
